Code reasoning plus scripts. Safe: in FinnhubClient._run, `self._ws = ws` and the `_get_symbols()` snapshot run with no await between them, so no reconcile can interleave between the new connection and the sent-set reset. A symbol newly wanted after the snapshot is subscribed once on the new ws; a symbol in the snapshot is not re-sent (it is in sent). A reconnect during an in-flight subscribe for a still-wanted symbol resubscribes it once on the new ws, and the old-connection completion only re-adds an existing entry. The "wanted but never subscribed" case (stale subscribe completing after the reset) is not reachable: browser ops are serialized by the manager lock, and the watchlist cannot shrink. Two divergences found, see bugs 1 and 2: (D) an unsubscribe that overtakes the connect-time resubscribe loop, which is realistic and reproduced with the real FinnhubClient; (C) a double subscribe that needs an old-connection call to complete successfully after the reconnect, which is contrived (a real closed ws raises, and failures keep state consistent). No path leaves a wanted symbol unsubscribed.

Diff (CR-normalized) of the two tests vs baseline: the only changes are the second call becoming asyncio.create_task + _yield and the final await becoming wait_for(gather(task, other), 5). The final assertion `s.upstream.subscribed == ["AAPL"]` is unchanged in both. They still test what their names say: browser suspended in upstream while a rule is created, and rule first then browser, each ending with exactly one subscribe. The restructure was needed because the lock-free path is gone, and the new queueing is the behaviour being checked. Both pass on current code (also in the 30x loop).

bug.description: Low/medium: a browser unsubscribe can overtake the connect-time resubscribe loop. On reconnect FinnhubClient sends subscribes one by one (awaiting each send) from a snapshot taken synchronously; _symbols_for_connect sets sent = snapshot immediately. If a browser leaves a browser-only symbol while the loop is still working through the list, _reconcile sees sent and not wanted and sends an unsubscribe on the new ws first; the loop then sends its stale subscribe afterwards. Result: the symbol stays subscribed upstream although wanted and sent are both empty, until the next reconnect (a leaked subscription that uses ticks and the free-tier symbol budget). Needs a browser disconnect in the narrow window of the resubscribe loop.
bug.reproduction: Real FinnhubClient with a fake connect whose ws.send yields (asyncio.sleep(0)); browser clients c1 subscribed to A and B (browser-only); start the client; as soon as the first subscribe (A) is on the wire call `await s.subscriptions.disconnect("c1")`. Wire order observed: subscribe A, unsubscribe B, subscribe B, unsubscribe A; net upstream subscribed = [B]; _upstream_sent = [] and upstream_symbols() = []. Scratch script was in the (now deleted) verifier temp dir.

bug.description: Low (contrived): an unsubscribe that is in flight on the old connection and completes successfully after a reconnect removes the symbol from the sent set, although the new connection was resubscribed with it (it was re-wanted by a rule before the reset). The queued reconcile then sends a second subscribe on the new connection (resubscribe + explicit subscribe). With a real websocket the old-connection call would raise instead, which keeps the state consistent, so this is only reachable with a client whose old-connection send can succeed late.
bug.reproduction: Recording upstream whose calls bind to the connection generation at call time and block on an Event; browser subscribes S; disconnect("c1") starts an unsubscribe (blocked); watch_symbol("S") queues; simulate reconnect by calling s._symbols_for_connect() (snapshot contains S); release the unsubscribe. Log: unsub S, resub S, sub S (a second subscribe on the new connection).

verification.self_critique: Windows only, Python 3.13, PG17. The reconnect divergences were shown with scripts and a fake ws, not a real Finnhub; the window in bug 1 depends on whether the real websockets send yields (it can). I did not run the frontend tests (untouched). The shutdown drain with a non-empty queue was not observed live. The fuzz uses a stub upstream with in-process latency, not network latency. Verdict is pass because all stated acceptance items hold and the two reconnect findings are low-severity edge cases the implementer's self-critique already flagged; the user may decide to require a fix for bug 1.
